instructions: Slice the pork against the grain, about 1/8 inch thick. Put it in a bowl.
Add 1 tbsp of the soy sauce, 1 tbsp of the oyster sauce, the sesame oil, 1/4 tsp of the white pepper and 1 tbsp of the cornstarch. Mix well with your hands and set it aside.
Slice the chili thinly and put it in a small bowl with the white vinegar. This is the chili vinegar for the table.
Mince the garlic. Slice the Chinese broccoli stems 1/2 inch thick and roughly chop the leaves, keeping them in two piles.
In a small bowl, stir the remaining 3 tbsp cornstarch into 1/4 cup cold water until smooth. This is the slurry.
Gently pull the noodles apart and toss them with the dark soy sauce.

Heat a large nonstick or cast iron skillet over high heat. Add 1 tbsp of the oil, then spread half the noodles in the pan. Leave them alone for 2 minutes, until the underside is browned in spots. Flip them and cook for 1 minute. Transfer to a platter.
Repeat with 1 tbsp oil and the rest of the noodles. Transfer them to the platter.
Turn the heat down to medium and add the last 2 tbsp oil. Add the soybean paste and stir for 30 seconds. Add the garlic and stir for 30 seconds, until it smells toasty.

Pour in the chicken broth and scrape up any browned bits from the pan. Add the remaining 1 1/2 tbsp soy sauce, the remaining 1 tbsp oyster sauce, the sugar and the remaining 1/4 tsp white pepper. Bring it to a boil over high heat.

Add the pork, pulling the slices apart as they go in, and the broccoli stems. Return to a boil and cook for 2 minutes. Add the leaves and cook for 1 minute, until the stems are bright green. You're cooking the pork to 145°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check a thick slice. No thermometer? Cut a slice open: it's done when there's no pink left.
Stir the slurry, then pour in half while stirring. Boil for 1 minute. If the gravy doesn't coat the back of a spoon, stir in the rest of the slurry and boil for 30 seconds.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Divide the noodles between four bowls and ladle the gravy over them. Serve with the chili vinegar.
method_notes: Both versions read build the dish the same way: sliced marinated pork, noodles charred in a hot pan with dark soy, and a starch-thickened gravy built on fermented soybean paste, garlic and Chinese broccoli. The lead uses pork stock and tapioca starch; this version uses chicken broth and cornstarch, and oyster sauce in place of Golden Mountain sauce, so nothing needs a special trip. The egg white in the pork marinade is dropped and the chili vinegar moves to the table.
